newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian jobs march banners make their point.
newsitem.headline: Belgian jobs march banners make their point.

text.p: "For swine fever they follow more rules than for us", one banner read.
If anyone was in any doubt about how Europe's factory workers feel about their treatment by governments and employers, Sunday's massive March for Jobs through Brussels should have opened their eyes.
The following are a few choice examples:
"Bosses have the right to live well, workers can die"
"All together for a Social Europe full of Employment"
"No to a Europe of money. For work and Social Europe"
French carmaker Renault and chairman Louis Schweitzer came in for particularly harsh treatment after the firm's shock decision two weeks ago to close its profitable plant at Vilvoorde near Brussels.
"It is five minutes to midnight Mr Schweitzer"
"After Renault, no one is safe any more"
One of the marchers carried a hanging effigy of Schweitzer while others repeatedly tossed a doll representing the Renault chief into the air and let it crash to the ground.
A giant wickerwork figure made Nazi salutes, and workers from Vilvoorde deposited a car chassis on the steps of the bourse and jumped on it.
